member.name: T:Althea.Arrays.BaseTensor`1
member.summary: The abstract tensor class with the only mutable that refers to the actual data storage. There may be more pointer(s) for different indices in a sparse tensor that inherits , but they shall be immutable.
member.typeparam: Any unmanaged struct as the data type
member.remarks:
Since the may be reference created quite frequently, storing the size as a C# is rather expensive.
Thus the C++ equivalent "struct { long size[16] }" of (which is a essentially a fixed long size[16]) is used instead to reduce the GC pressure.
Also, the has no finalizer and if it is composed of which still has no finalizer, the instance stays in GC generation 0 which is quite fast in deallocation.
Therefore, the derived class shall follow the same strategy, such as .

member.name: T:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseVectorFormat
member.summary: The enum indicates the format specification of a sparse vector. Each bit flag indicates an atomic format.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseVectorFormat.Coordinated
member.summary: The Coordinate Format that stores each non-zero element and its zero-based index in separate storages.
member.remarks: For default implementations, this is the only supported sparse vector format

member.name: T:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat
member.summary: The enum indicates the format specification of a sparse matrix. Each bit flag indicates an atomic format.
member.remarks:
All the internally defined formats are 3-array variations rather than 4-array ones.
All non-compressed formats shall lies within the left-most 16 bits, and compressed ones shall lies within the right-most 16 bits.
All the row major formats shall lies within the even bits, and column major ones shall lies within the odd bits.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.COOR
member.summary: Coordinate Row-major Format (COR) that stores each non-zero element's x and y coordinates which are sorted in the row-first order.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.COOC
member.summary: Coordinate Column-major Format (COC) that stores each non-zero element's x and y coordinates which are sorted in the column-first order. The transpose of a format is the format.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.BCOR
member.summary: Block Coordinate Row-major Format (BCOR) that stores each non-zero block's x and y coordinates which are sorted in the row-first order.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.BCOC
member.summary: Block Coordinate Column-major Format (BCOR) that stores each non-zero block's x and y coordinates which are sorted in the column-first order.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.CSC
member.summary: Compressed Sparse Column Format (CSC). The only way the differs from the format is that the column index array instead of row index array stores the end-of-column (not end-of-row) offsets. The transpose of a format is the format.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.CSR
member.summary: Compressed Sparse Row Format (CSR). The only way the differs from the format is that the array containing the row indices is compressed, that is, the row index array only stores the end-of-row offsets with size == number_of_rows + 1 whose first element is 0.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.BSC
member.summary: Block Sparse Column Format (BSC). The only way the differs from the format is that the column index array instead of row index array stores the end-of-column (not end-of-row) offsets of blocks. The transpose of a format is the format.

member.name: F:Althea.LinearAlgebra.Sparse.SparseMatrixFormat.BSR
member.summary: Block Sparse Row Format (BSR). The only way the differs from the format is that instead of indexing values, indexes the dense block sub-matrices. Therefore, this requires additional parameters: number of non-zero blocks instead of non-zero values, number of block matrix rows, number of block matrix columns, end-of-row offsets are counted in blocks and therefore is of size == number_of_rows / block_rows + 1.

member.name: T:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy
member.summary: The indicates which strategy shall be adopted by the thick restart Krylov subspace algorithms.
member.remarks: Other non built-in strategies are possible and they work as long as there exists implementation supporting them.

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy.Naive
member.summary: The naïve strategy which only preserve the lowest Ritz eigen-pair and converged ones.

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy.IndexBased
member.summary:
Based on the index of Ritz eigen-pairs, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=n_c+\min{\left\{n_{\mathrm{eig}},\left(p-n_c\right)\left(\frac{2}{5}+\frac{n_{\mathrm{eig}}}{10p}\right)\right\}}$$

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy.CurrentResidualBest
member.summary:
Based on the residual of Ritz eigen-pairs, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=\underset{i}{\mathrm{argmax}}\left( \left| s_{n,i} \right| < \max\left\{ \sqrt{\left| s_{n,n_{\mathrm{eig}}} \right|\max_{j}\left| s_{n,j} \right|},2\left| s_{n,n_{\mathrm{eig}}} \right| \right\} \right)$$

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy.OneStepResidualImprove
member.summary:
Based on the improvement of residual of Ritz eigen-pairs of single iteration after the restart, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=\max{\left\{n_{\mathrm{eig}},\frac{3p+2n_c}{5}\right\}}$$

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy.WholeIterResidualImprove
member.summary:
Based on the improvement of residual of Ritz eigen-pairs of single iteration after the restart, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=\underset{k}{\max}{\left(p-k\right)\frac{\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_1}{\lambda_m-\lambda_1}}$$

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.RestartStrategy.KrylovSchur
member.summary: The heuristic used by Krylov-Schur algorithm to prevent stagnating

member.name: T:Althea.Solver.ReorthogonalizeMethod
member.summary: The indicates which method shall be used to re-orthogonalize with the previous basis in Krylov subspace algorithms.
member.remarks: Other non built-in methods are possible and they work as long as there exists implementation supporting them.

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.ReorthogonalizeMethod.None
member.summary: Do not perform re-orthogonalization, this may lead to serious problems, e.g. Lanczos may never converge

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.ReorthogonalizeMethod.Selective
member.summary: Selective re-orthogonalize, let the internal heuristic to determine when and which basis to re-orthogonalize

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.ReorthogonalizeMethod.Full
member.summary: Perform full re-orthogonalization at each iteration, this may lead to extra performance loss, especially when the problem size is small. You can use this method when the one does not perform well

member.name: F:Althea.Solver.ReorthogonalizeMethod.RobustFull

member.name: F:Althea.TensorAlgebra.Sparse.SparseTensorFormat.BlockCoordinated
member.summary:
The Block Coordinated Sparse Format that divides the tensor into block tensors of fixed size and store their zero-based indices in a storage.
This is similar to the .

member.name: F:Althea.TensorAlgebra.Sparse.SparseTensorFormat.VariableBlockCoordinated
member.summary:
The Variable Block Sparse Format that only differs from by letting the block tensors have variable sizes while the alignments are still necessary.
Therefore the implementation shall contains an extra (size == rank) array whose elements are aligned lengths (or accumulated ones) of corresponding dimensions.
